drug_class: Dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (wake-promoting agent)
purpose: Solriamfetol is used to help people who feel excessively sleepy during the day due to narcolepsy or obstructive sleep apnea. It helps you stay awake and more alert so you can go about your daily activities. It does not cure the underlying sleep condition but helps manage the daytime sleepiness.
how_it_works: This medication works by boosting the levels of two natural chemicals in your brain called dopamine and norepinephrine. These chemicals help promote wakefulness and keep you feeling alert. Think of it like giving your brain a gentle nudge to stay in 'awake mode' during the day.
common_side_effects: Headache, nausea, decreased appetite, dry mouth, feeling anxious or jittery, trouble sleeping if taken too late in the day, and increased heart rate or blood pressure.
warnings: This medication can raise your blood pressure and heart rate, so your doctor will monitor these regularly. It should not be taken within 9 hours of bedtime because it can cause insomnia. It has a potential for abuse and dependence, so use it exactly as prescribed. Avoid it if you have severe heart problems or have taken an MAO inhibitor (a type of antidepressant) in the past 14 days. Tell your doctor if you have anxiety, a history of substance abuse, or kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: For narcolepsy, the usual starting dose is 75 mg taken once in the morning, which may be increased to 150 mg once daily if needed. For sleep apnea, the starting dose is typically 37.5 mg once in the morning, and it can be increased up to 150 mg daily. Always take it in the morning to avoid sleep problems at night.
